data.narrative:
SambaNova Systems is a Series A-stage semiconductor design company founded by Rodrigo Liang, Kunle Olukotun, and Christopher Ré. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 3 public semiconductors (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage comparables, with immediate peer benchmarks including Rebellions, d-Matrix, and Positron AI.

Two triangulation methods apply to this valuation. Stage-Progression analysis, anchoring to the $11.0B last post-money valuation, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, implying $22.0B. Peer-Median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies yields a median valuation of $2.0B, with a range from $1.0B (Positron AI, Series B) to $2.3B (Rebellions, Series A). Public-Comp anchoring via P/S multiples cannot be applied; the public semiconductor universe trades at a 20.5x median multiple, but SambaNova's revenue is not disclosed.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $1.7B to $25.3B, with a median of $12.0B. The wide dispersion reflects material tension between the Stage-Progression method's $22.0B and peer-median's $2.0B, suggesting the current $11.0B valuation sits between these anchors. Key uncertainties include whether SambaNova's technology differentiation and capital intensity justify a premium to seed-stage peer multiples, and whether the 2.0x step-up reflects realistic market conditions for unfunded frontier semiconductor plays.
